from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout with title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout(
            "Foundation: The Power of Three (Ternary)", 
            [
                "Binary uses two states, but ternary uses three.", 
                "Ternary digits represent states zero, one, and two.", 
                "Positional values are powers of three: one, three, nine.", 
                "Three-state switches generate twenty-seven unique configurations.", 
                "This base-3 system coordinates our entire logical map."
            ]
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        # Visualizing the difference (Binary vs Ternary labels)
        binary_label = Text("Binary: {0, 1}", font_size=24, color="#AAAAAA")
        ternary_label = Text("Ternary: {0, 1, 2}", font_size=24, color="#FFFFFF")
        
        self.place_at_grid(binary_label, "A3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(ternary_label, "B3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(binary_label), FadeIn(ternary_label))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Display three circles labeled 0, 1, and 2
        circle_0 = Circle(radius=0.4, color=WHITE)
        circle_1 = Circle(radius=0.4, color=WHITE)
        circle_2 = Circle(radius=0.4, color=WHITE)
        
        label_0 = Text("0", font_size=30)
        label_1 = Text("1", font_size=30)
        label_2 = Text("2", font_size=30)
        
        group_0 = VGroup(circle_0, label_0)
        group_1 = VGroup(circle_1, label_1)
        group_2 = VGroup(circle_2, label_2)
        
        self.place_at_grid(group_0, "C2")
        self.place_at_grid(group_1, "C3")
        self.place_at_grid(group_2, "C4")
        
        self.play(Create(group_0), Create(group_1), Create(group_2))
        
        # Sequentially highlight
        self.play(circle_0.animate.set_color("#00FF00"), label_0.animate.set_color("#00FF00"), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(circle_1.animate.set_color("#FFFF00"), label_1.animate.set_color("#FFFF00"), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(circle_2.animate.set_color("#FF0000"), label_2.animate.set_color("#FF0000"), run_time=0.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Show magnitude labels: 3^2, 3^1, and 3^0 in #00FFFF
        mag_2 = Text("3²", color="#00FFFF", font_size=36)
        mag_1 = Text("3¹", color="#00FFFF", font_size=36)
        mag_0 = Text("3⁰", color="#00FFFF", font_size=36)
        
        self.place_at_grid(mag_2, "D2")
        self.place_at_grid(mag_1, "D3")
        self.place_at_grid(mag_0, "D4")
        
        mag_vals = VGroup(
            Text("(9)", font_size=20, color="#00FFFF"),
            Text("(3)", font_size=20, color="#00FFFF"),
            Text("(1)", font_size=20, color="#00FFFF")
        )
        
        # Offset them slightly below the powers
        self.place_at_grid(mag_vals[0], "D2").shift(DOWN*0.4)
        self.place_at_grid(mag_vals[1], "D3").shift(DOWN*0.4)
        self.place_at_grid(mag_vals[2], "D4").shift(DOWN*0.4)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(mag_2), FadeIn(mag_1), FadeIn(mag_0))
        self.play(Write(mag_vals))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Place digits '2', '1', and '0' under labels
        digit_2 = Text("2", font_size=42, color="#FFFFFF")
        digit_1 = Text("1", font_size=42, color="#FFFFFF")
        digit_0 = Text("0", font_size=42, color="#FFFFFF")
        
        self.place_at_grid(digit_2, "E2")
        self.place_at_grid(digit_1, "E3")
        self.place_at_grid(digit_0, "E4")
        
        # Show the calculation 2*9 + 1*3 + 0*1
        calc_text = Text("2 × 9 + 1 × 3 + 0 × 1", font_size=28, color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_in_area(calc_text, "F2", "F5")
        
        self.play(Write(digit_2), Write(digit_1), Write(digit_0))
        self.play(FadeIn(calc_text))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Transform the ternary digits into decimal '21' and flash it
        result_21 = Text("= 21", font_size=42, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(result_21, "E5")
        
        final_group = VGroup(digit_2, digit_1, digit_0, calc_text, result_21)
        
        decimal_box = Text("Decimal: 21", font_size=48, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(decimal_box, "D2", "F5")
        
        self.play(Write(result_21))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(final_group, decimal_box),
            FadeOut(group_0), FadeOut(group_1), FadeOut(group_2),
            FadeOut(mag_2), FadeOut(mag_1), FadeOut(mag_0), FadeOut(mag_vals),
            FadeOut(binary_label), FadeOut(ternary_label)
        )
        self.play(Indicate(decimal_box, color=WHITE, scale_factor=1.2))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup title and lecture lines
        title_str = "The Rule Change: Constrained Towers of Hanoi"
        lines_str = [
            'Classic Hanoi allows moves between any two pegs.',
            'We restrict moves to adjacent pegs only.',
            'Moving from peg zero to two requires intermediate steps.',
            'This constraint creates a specific, predictable recursive path.',
            'Every legal transition follows this strict linear rule.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_str, lines_str)
        
        # Colors
        PEG_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"
        DISK_COLOR = "#FF8C00"
        X_COLOR = "#FF0000"
        ARROW_COLOR = "#00FF00"
        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = "#FFFF00"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight first line
        self.lecture[0].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        # Create Pegs
        peg0 = Line(self.grid["B2"], self.grid["E2"], color=PEG_COLOR, stroke_width=6)
        peg1 = Line(self.grid["B4"], self.grid["E4"], color=PEG_COLOR, stroke_width=6)
        peg2 = Line(self.grid["B6"], self.grid["E6"], color=PEG_COLOR, stroke_width=6)
        
        label0 = Text("0", color=PEG_COLOR, font_size=24)
        label1 = Text("1", color=PEG_COLOR, font_size=24)
        label2 = Text("2", color=PEG_COLOR, font_size=24)
        
        self.place_at_grid(label0, "F2")
        self.place_at_grid(label1, "F4")
        self.place_at_grid(label2, "F6")
        
        # Create Disk
        disk = Rectangle(width=0.8, height=0.3, fill_color=DISK_COLOR, fill_opacity=1.0, stroke_color=DISK_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(disk, "E2")
        
        self.play(
            Create(peg0), Create(peg1), Create(peg2),
            FadeIn(label0), FadeIn(label1), FadeIn(label2),
            FadeIn(disk)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        # Show adjacency connections (implied by layout, but let's highlight neighbors)
        adj_line1 = Line(self.grid["D2"], self.grid["D4"], color=PEG_COLOR, stroke_opacity=0.3)
        adj_line2 = Line(self.grid["D4"], self.grid["D6"], color=PEG_COLOR, stroke_opacity=0.3)
        
        self.play(Create(adj_line1), Create(adj_line2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        # Draw a forbidden direct path from 0 to 2
        forbidden_arc = ArcBetweenPoints(self.grid["B2"], self.grid["B6"], angle=-TAU/4, color=X_COLOR, stroke_opacity=0.5)
        
        # Red X
        x_line1 = Line(self.grid["C3"], self.grid["D5"], color=X_COLOR, stroke_width=8)
        x_line2 = Line(self.grid["D3"], self.grid["C5"], color=X_COLOR, stroke_width=8)
        forbidden_x = VGroup(x_line1, x_line2)
        
        self.play(Create(forbidden_arc), Create(forbidden_x))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        # Animate disk moving from Peg 0 to Peg 1
        arrow1 = Arrow(self.grid["C2"], self.grid["C4"], color=ARROW_COLOR, buff=0.1)
        
        # Move disk sequence: Up -> Over -> Down
        target_pos_0_top = self.grid["A2"]
        target_pos_1_top = self.grid["A4"]
        target_pos_1_bottom = self.grid["E4"]
        
        self.play(
            disk.animate.move_to(target_pos_0_top),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        self.play(
            disk.animate.move_to(target_pos_1_top),
            GrowArrow(arrow1),
            run_time=0.7
        )
        self.play(
            disk.animate.move_to(target_pos_1_bottom),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        # Animate disk moving from Peg 1 to Peg 2
        arrow2 = Arrow(self.grid["C4"], self.grid["C6"], color=ARROW_COLOR, buff=0.1)
        
        target_pos_2_top = self.grid["A6"]
        target_pos_2_bottom = self.grid["E6"]
        
        self.play(
            disk.animate.move_to(target_pos_1_top),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        self.play(
            disk.animate.move_to(target_pos_2_top),
            GrowArrow(arrow2),
            run_time=0.7
        )
        self.play(
            disk.animate.move_to(target_pos_2_bottom),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "Mapping States to Geometry", 
            [
                'Every valid disk configuration is a graph vertex.', 
                'Lines connect states reachable by one legal move.', 
                'One disk creates a simple line of three states.'
            ]
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Create 3 dots for 1-disk states
        dot_0 = Dot(color="#00FFFF", radius=0.1)
        dot_1 = Dot(color="#00FFFF", radius=0.1)
        dot_2 = Dot(color="#00FFFF", radius=0.1)
        
        self.place_at_grid(dot_0, "C2")
        self.place_at_grid(dot_1, "C3")
        self.place_at_grid(dot_2, "C4")
        
        label_0 = Text("0", font_size=18).next_to(dot_0, DOWN, buff=0.2)
        label_1 = Text("1", font_size=18).next_to(dot_1, DOWN, buff=0.2)
        label_2 = Text("2", font_size=18).next_to(dot_2, DOWN, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(dot_0), FadeIn(dot_1), FadeIn(dot_2),
            Write(label_0), Write(label_1), Write(label_2)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Connect dots with white lines
        line_01 = Line(dot_0.get_center(), dot_1.get_center(), color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        line_12 = Line(dot_1.get_center(), dot_2.get_center(), color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        
        self.play(Create(line_01), Create(line_12))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Clear the 1-disk visualization to make room for the 2-disk triangle
        self.play(
            FadeOut(dot_0, dot_1, dot_2, label_0, label_1, label_2, line_01, line_12)
        )

        # Define 9 vertices for 2-disk states (Disk2, Disk1)
        # Groups based on Disk 2 position
        # Group 2 (Top): A3, B3, B4
        v22 = Dot(color="#00FFFF", radius=0.08) # Disk2=2, Disk1=2
        v20 = Dot(color="#00FFFF", radius=0.08) # Disk2=2, Disk1=0
        v21 = Dot(color="#00FFFF", radius=0.08) # Disk2=2, Disk1=1
        
        # Group 0 (Bottom-Left): D1, E1, E2
        v00 = Dot(color="#00FFFF", radius=0.08) # Disk2=0, Disk1=0
        v01 = Dot(color="#00FFFF", radius=0.08) # Disk2=0, Disk1=1
        v02 = Dot(color="#00FFFF", radius=0.08) # Disk2=0, Disk1=2
        
        # Group 1 (Bottom-Right): D6, E5, E6
        v11 = Dot(color="#00FFFF", radius=0.08) # Disk2=1, Disk1=1
        v12 = Dot(color="#00FFFF", radius=0.08) # Disk2=1, Disk1=2
        v10 = Dot(color="#00FFFF", radius=0.08) # Disk2=1, Disk1=0

        self.place_at_grid(v22, "A3")
        self.place_at_grid(v20, "B3")
        self.place_at_grid(v21, "B4")
        
        self.place_at_grid(v00, "D1")
        self.place_at_grid(v01, "E1")
        self.place_at_grid(v02, "E2")
        
        self.place_at_grid(v11, "D6")
        self.place_at_grid(v12, "E6")
        self.place_at_grid(v10, "E5")

        # Inner connections (Move Disk 1)
        inner_lines = [
            Line(v22.get_center(), v20.get_center(), color=WHITE, stroke_width=1.5),
            Line(v20.get_center(), v21.get_center(), color=WHITE, stroke_width=1.5),
            Line(v00.get_center(), v01.get_center(), color=WHITE, stroke_width=1.5),
            Line(v01.get_center(), v02.get_center(), color=WHITE, stroke_width=1.5),
            Line(v11.get_center(), v12.get_center(), color=WHITE, stroke_width=1.5),
            Line(v12.get_center(), v10.get_center(), color=WHITE, stroke_width=1.5)
        ]

        # Labels for groups (Disk 2 position)
        g2_label = Text("Disk 2 at 2", font_size=14).next_to(v22, UP, buff=0.1)
        g0_label = Text("Disk 2 at 0", font_size=14).next_to(v01, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        g1_label = Text("Disk 2 at 1", font_size=14).next_to(v12, DOWN, buff=0.1)

        self.play(
            AnimationGroup(
                *[FadeIn(v) for v in [v22, v20, v21, v00, v01, v02, v11, v12, v10]],
                *[Create(l) for l in inner_lines],
                Write(g2_label), Write(g0_label), Write(g1_label),
                lag_ratio=0.1
            )
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # Bridge edges (Move Disk 2)
        bridge_lines = [
            Line(v20.get_center(), v02.get_center(), color=WHITE, stroke_width=1.5), # Move Disk 2 between 2 and 0
            Line(v01.get_center(), v10.get_center(), color=WHITE, stroke_width=1.5), # Move Disk 2 between 0 and 1
            Line(v12.get_center(), v21.get_center(), color=WHITE, stroke_width=1.5)  # Move Disk 2 between 1 and 2
        ]

        self.play(*[Create(bl) for bl in bridge_lines])
        self.wait(1)

        # Highlight specific vertex and show configuration
        # Highlight (Disk2=2, Disk1=1) -> v21
        highlight_circle = Circle(radius=0.2, color=YELLOW).move_to(v21.get_center())
        
        # Disk Config Window
        window_bg = Rectangle(width=2.5, height=1.5, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.1)
        self.place_in_area(window_bg, "C4", "D5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Simple Pegs and Disks (State: Disk 2 on Peg 2, Disk 1 on Peg 1)
        p0 = Line(UP*0.3, DOWN*0.3, color=GRAY).shift(window_bg.get_center() + LEFT*0.6)
        p1 = Line(UP*0.3, DOWN*0.3, color=GRAY).shift(window_bg.get_center())
        p2 = Line(UP*0.3, DOWN*0.3, color=GRAY).shift(window_bg.get_center() + RIGHT*0.6)
        
        d2 = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.05, width=0.4, height=0.1, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.8).move_to(p2.get_start() + DOWN*0.5)
        d1 = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.05, width=0.2, height=0.1, color=RED, fill_opacity=0.8).move_to(p1.get_start() + DOWN*0.5)
        
        config_group = VGroup(window_bg, p0, p1, p2, d2, d1)
        
        self.play(Create(highlight_circle), FadeIn(config_group))
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Final Highlight: Clean up and show full structure
        self.play(
            FadeOut(highlight_circle), 
            FadeOut(config_group),
            FadeOut(g2_label, g0_label, g1_label)
        )
        
        # Highlight resulting 9-vertex structure
        all_dots = VGroup(v22, v20, v21, v00, v01, v02, v11, v12, v10)
        all_lines = VGroup(*inner_lines, *bridge_lines)
        
        self.play(
            all_dots.animate.set_color(WHITE),
            all_lines.animate.set_stroke(width=3)
        )
        self.wait(2)
        
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup basic layout
        lines = [
            "Adding more disks expands the state-space graph recursively.",
            "Two disks form three connected triangles of states.",
            "Increasing disks reveals the iconic Sierpinski Triangle fractal.",
            "Corners represent all disks stacked on a single peg.",
            "The fractal structure perfectly captures the game's logic."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Emergence of the Sierpinski Triangle", lines)

        # Helper to generate Sierpinski vertices
        def get_sierpinski_vertices(level, center, side_length):
            if level == 0:
                return [center]
            
            h = side_length * np.sqrt(3) / 2
            # Vertices of the large triangle container
            v0 = center + np.array([0, h/2, 0])      # Top
            v1 = center + np.array([-side_length/2, -h/2, 0]) # Bottom Left
            v2 = center + np.array([side_length/2, -h/2, 0])  # Bottom Right
            
            # Distance from center of container to centers of sub-triangles
            # The sub-triangle centers are midpoints between container center and vertices
            # But for perfect packing, they are shifted by side_length/4
            offset = side_length / 4
            c0 = center + np.array([0, (h/2) / 2, 0])
            c1 = center + np.array([-side_length/4, -(h/4), 0])
            c2 = center + np.array([side_length/4, -(h/4), 0])
            
            res = []
            res.extend(get_sierpinski_vertices(level - 1, v0 - np.array([0, h/4, 0]), side_length / 2))
            res.extend(get_sierpinski_vertices(level - 1, v1 + np.array([side_length/4, h/4, 0]), side_length / 2))
            res.extend(get_sierpinski_vertices(level - 1, v2 + np.array([-side_length/4, h/4, 0]), side_length / 2))
            return res

        # Manual Sierpinski Graph Logic for level 2 (9 nodes)
        def create_graph_level_2(center, size):
            h = size * np.sqrt(3) / 2
            # 3 clusters of 3 nodes
            # Each cluster is a triangle
            sub_size = size / 2
            sub_h = sub_size * np.sqrt(3) / 2
            
            # Centers for the 3 sub-triangles
            c_top = center + np.array([0, h/4, 0])
            c_bl = center + np.array([-size/4, -h/4, 0])
            c_br = center + np.array([size/4, -h/4, 0])
            
            def get_tri_verts(c, s):
                sh = s * np.sqrt(3) / 2
                return [c + np.array([0, sh/2, 0]), c + np.array([-s/2, -sh/2, 0]), c + np.array([s/2, -sh/2, 0])]

            v_top = get_tri_verts(c_top, sub_size/2)
            v_bl = get_tri_verts(c_bl, sub_size/2)
            v_br = get_tri_verts(c_br, sub_size/2)
            
            all_verts = v_top + v_bl + v_br
            nodes = VGroup(*[Dot(p, radius=0.06, color="#87CEEB") for p in all_verts])
            
            edges = VGroup()
            # Inner triangle edges
            for i in range(0, 9, 3):
                edges.add(Line(all_verts[i], all_verts[i+1], stroke_width=2, color=WHITE))
                edges.add(Line(all_verts[i+1], all_verts[i+2], stroke_width=2, color=WHITE))
                edges.add(Line(all_verts[i+2], all_verts[i], stroke_width=2, color=WHITE))
            
            # Bridge edges for Level 2
            edges.add(Line(all_verts[1], all_verts[3], stroke_width=2, color=WHITE)) # top-left to bl-top
            edges.add(Line(all_verts[2], all_verts[6], stroke_width=2, color=WHITE)) # top-right to br-top
            edges.add(Line(all_verts[5], all_verts[7], stroke_width=2, color=WHITE)) # bl-right to br-left
            
            return VGroup(nodes, edges)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        # Show Level 2 graph (2-disk state space)
        g2 = create_graph_level_2(ORIGIN, 3.0)
        self.place_in_area(g2, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(g2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        # Highlight the three sub-triangles
        self.play(g2[1].animate.set_stroke(color="#00FF00", opacity=0.5))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Construct Level 3 (27 nodes) by triplicating Level 2
        g2_copy = g2.copy()
        target_size = 4.0
        h_total = target_size * np.sqrt(3) / 2
        center_area = self.grid["D3.5"] if "D3.5" in self.grid else np.array([3.0, 0, 0])
        # Use place_in_area to find center
        dummy = Mobject()
        self.place_in_area(dummy, "A1", "F6")
        main_center = dummy.get_center()

        c_top = main_center + np.array([0, h_total/4, 0])
        c_bl = main_center + np.array([-target_size/4, -h_total/4, 0])
        c_br = main_center + np.array([target_size/4, -h_total/4, 0])

        g3_top = g2.copy().scale(0.5).move_to(c_top)
        g3_bl = g2.copy().scale(0.5).move_to(c_bl)
        g3_br = g2.copy().scale(0.5).move_to(c_br)

        # New bridge edges for Level 3
        # We need specific vertices. For Level 2 (scaled), the corner indices are:
        # 0 (top), 4 (bottom-left), 8 (bottom-right)
        bridge_edges = VGroup(
            Line(g3_top[0][1].get_center(), g3_bl[0][0].get_center(), color="#FFD700", stroke_width=3),
            Line(g3_top[0][2].get_center(), g3_br[0][0].get_center(), color="#FFD700", stroke_width=3),

        self.play(

        self.play(Create(bridge_edges))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):

        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Ternary numbers act as addresses for every puzzle state.",
            "Solving the puzzle means traversing the fractal's edges.",
            "The longest path follows the triangle's outer perimeter."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Fractal Traversal via Ternary Addresses", lecture_lines)

        # --- Data Generation ---
        def get_pos_normalized(addr):
            # Triangle corners (normalized)
            p0 = np.array([0, 1, 0])      # Top
            p1 = np.array([-0.866, -0.5, 0])  # BL
            p2 = np.array([0.866, -0.5, 0])   # BR
            
            curr_p0, curr_p1, curr_p2 = p0, p1, p2
            for char in addr:
                m01 = (curr_p0 + curr_p1) / 2
                m12 = (curr_p1 + curr_p2) / 2
                m20 = (curr_p2 + curr_p0) / 2
                if char == '0':
                    curr_p1, curr_p2 = m01, m20
                elif char == '1':
                    curr_p0, curr_p2 = m01, m12
                else: # '2'
                    curr_p0, curr_p1 = m20, m12
            return (curr_p0 + curr_p1 + curr_p2) / 3

        addresses = [np.base_repr(i, base=3).zfill(3) for i in range(27)]
        normalized_points = [get_pos_normalized(addr) for addr in addresses]
        
        # Dots representing states
        state_dots = VGroup(*[Dot(p, radius=0.03, color=GRAY) for p in normalized_points])
        self.place_in_area(state_dots, 'A2', 'F6', scale_factor=2.0)
        
        # Extract mapped positions
        real_points = [dot.get_center() for dot in state_dots]

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        
        # Display the "Address System" label
        address_label = Text("Current Address:", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(address_label, "A2")
        
        # Initial counter
        counter = Text(addresses[0], font_size=32, color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(counter, "A3")
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(state_dots),
            Write(address_label),
            Write(counter)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00")
        )
        
        # We'll trace the path. For performance, we'll draw it in chunks.
        path_lines = VGroup()
        
        for i in range(26):
            start_p = real_points[i]
            end_p = real_points[i+1]
            line = Line(start_p, end_p, color="#00FF00", stroke_width=5)
            path_lines.add(line)
            
            # Create updated counter text
            new_counter = Text(addresses[i+1], font_size=32, color="#FFFF00")
            new_counter.move_to(counter)
            
            # Animate in small steps
            self.add(line)
            self.remove(counter)
            self.add(new_counter)
            counter = new_counter
            
            # Slow down slightly for visual clarity every few steps
            if i % 5 == 0:
                self.wait(0.1)
            else:
                self.wait(0.05)

        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF")
        )
        
        # Highlight the corners to show it's the "longest path" from corner to corner
        corner_000 = Dot(real_points[0], radius=0.1, color=WHITE)
        corner_222 = Dot(real_points[-1], radius=0.1, color=WHITE)
        
        solved_text = Text("Puzzle Solved", font_size=36, color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(solved_text, "F3")

        self.play(
            Flash(corner_000, color=WHITE),
            Flash(corner_222, color=WHITE),
            Write(solved_text)
        )
        
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Trinity of Logic: Ternary, Towers, and Triangles
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate Computer Science or Mathematics students

sections.title: Foundation: The Power of Three (Ternary)
sections.content: Introduce the Base-3 (ternary) counting system. Explain how each digit represents a state (0, 1, or 2) and how position indicates magnitude ($3^0, 3^1, 3^2$). This serves as the 'coordinate system' for the entire lesson.
sections.example: Visualize a 3-state light switch: 'Off' (0), 'Dim' (1), and 'Bright' (2). Counting from 0 to 8 in ternary (000 to 222) represents all possible configurations of 3 such switches.

sections.title: The Rule Change: Constrained Towers of Hanoi
sections.content: Introduce the 'Linear' or 'Constrained' Towers of Hanoi. Unlike the classic version, disks can only move between ADJACENT pegs (Peg 0 ↔ Peg 1 ↔ Peg 2). To move from Peg 0 to Peg 2, a disk must stop at Peg 1 first. This constraint forces a specific, recursive path.
sections.example: Imagine three rooms in a line (Living Room, Hallway, Bedroom). You cannot teleport a heavy sofa from the Living Room to the Bedroom; it must pass through the Hallway.

sections.title: Mapping States to Geometry
sections.content: Define a 'State' as the position of $n$ disks. Represent every possible valid configuration of disks as a vertex (dot) on a graph. Connect vertices with lines if a single legal move can transition one state to another. This transforms a logic puzzle into a geometric map.
sections.example: With 1 disk, the map is a simple line: State [0]—[1]—[2]. With 2 disks, the map starts to branch, forming small triangles.

sections.title: Emergence of the Sierpinski Triangle
sections.content: Demonstrate that as the number of disks ($n$) increases, the state-space graph of the constrained Hanoi puzzle perfectly forms a Sierpinski Triangle. Each larger triangle is composed of three smaller versions of itself, representing the placement of the largest disk on Peg 0, 1, or 2.
sections.example: Zoom out from a 1-disk line to a 3-disk fractal. Show that the 'corners' of the Sierpinski Triangle represent all disks stacked on a single peg (000, 111, or 222 in ternary).

sections.title: Fractal Traversal via Ternary Addresses
sections.content: Synthesize the concepts. Show how a ternary number acts as a 'GPS address' to find any state on the Sierpinski Triangle. Traversing the edges of the triangle is equivalent to solving the puzzle. The longest path (from Peg 0 to Peg 2) follows the outer boundary of the fractal.
sections.example: A digital ant needs to move from the 'All-on-0' corner to the 'All-on-2' corner. By following the ternary sequence (000 → 001 → ... → 222), the ant traces the zig-zag perimeter of the Sierpinski gasket.

[VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: The disk and the 'Classic Hanoi' red arc reach Row A during movement, which crowds the title text at the top of the frame. Fix: Line 85: self.place_at_grid(disk, 'E2', scale_factor=0.7) and constrain movement pathing to peak at Row B. (line=85, object=disk)

[VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: Numeric labels 0, 1, and 2 are at the bottom grid edge (Row F) and appear detached from the peg bases at Row E. Fix: Line 79: self.place_at_grid(label0, 'F2', scale_factor=0.8); Line 80: self.place_at_grid(label1, 'F4', scale_factor=0.8); Line 81: self.place_at_grid(label2, 'F6', scale_factor=0.8) (line=79, object=label0, label1, label2)

[VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: The red 'X' restriction symbol overlaps with the middle peg at C4, creating visual clutter and potentially obscuring the peg line. Fix: Reposition the restriction symbol to B4 (red: #FF0000) to align with the peak of the forbidden jump arc, keeping it clear of the peg. (object=red_x_symbol)

[VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: The corner label '111' within the 'dummy' group overlaps and obstructs the fifth lecture line ('The fractal structure...'), specifically the word 'logic'. Fix: Line 147: self.place_in_area(dummy, 'B1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6) (line=147, object=dummy)

[VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: The state-space graph 'g2' is scaled too large and positioned too far to the left, causing visual crowding with the lecture text and leaving no margin. Fix: Line 125: self.place_in_area(g2, 'B1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6) (line=125, object=g2)

[VideoCritic][section_5] Problem: The address_label and counter at A2 and A3 overlap, causing 'Current Address' to be obscured by the numerical value. Fix: Line 90: self.place_at_grid('A2', scale_factor=0.8); Line 94: self.place_at_grid('A5', scale_factor=0.8) (line=94, object=counter)

[VideoCritic][section_5] Problem: The state_dots fractal area (A2-F6) is too large, overlapping with the labels in the top header row (Row A). Fix: Line 80: self.place_in_area('B2', 'E6', scale_factor=1.5) (line=80, object=state_dots)

[VideoCritic][section_5] Problem: The solved_text ('Puzzle Solved') at F3 is positioned too close to the bottom edge of the fractal's traversal path. Fix: Line 147: self.place_at_grid('F3', scale_factor=0.9) (line=147, object=solved_text)

[VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: Overlap in Row D. Power labels (mag_2/1/0) and magnitude values (mag_vals) both occupy grid cells D2, D3, and D4. Fix: Move power labels to Row C (Line 109-111): self.place_at_grid(mag_2, 'C2'); self.place_at_grid(mag_1, 'C3'); self.place_at_grid(mag_0, 'C4'). Note: This will require moving the objects currently in Row C.

[VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: Vertical chain conflict. Shifting powers to Row C (per Issue 37) creates an overlap with the circular containers (group_0/1/2). Fix: Move circular containers to Row B (Lines 88-90): self.place_at_grid(group_0, 'B2'); self.place_at_grid(group_1, 'B3'); self.place_at_grid(group_2, 'B4').

[VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: Inefficient header layout. Binary and ternary labels occupy separate rows (A and B), wasting vertical space. Fix: Place both on Row A (Lines 65-66): self.place_at_grid(binary_label, 'A2', scale_factor=0.8); self.place_at_grid(ternary_label, 'A4', scale_factor=0.8).

[VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: The window_bg element (puzzle state image) at C4-D5 significantly overlaps graph edges and vertices of the right-hand cluster. Fix: Reposition and scale: self.place_in_area(window_bg, 'C3', 'D4', scale_factor=0.7) (Line 169).

[VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: The initial three dots (dot_0, dot_1, dot_2) occupy the center (Row C), causing clutter with the subsequent graph. Fix: Move initial dots to Row B (Line 65-67): self.place_at_grid(dot_0, 'B2', scale_factor=0.8); self.place_at_grid(dot_1, 'B3', scale_factor=0.8); self.place_at_grid(dot_2, 'B4', scale_factor=0.8).

[VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: Vertex cluster (v11, v12, v10) at the extreme right edge (D6, E6, E5) risks labels being cut off. Fix: Shift the cluster inwards (adjust positions for v11, v12, v10 to D5, E5, E4 area or equivalent to ensure safety margin).
